title: TrailGenic Sleep Science Endurance Dataset
description: Shell dataset module modeling sleep-dependent recovery and endurance adaptation.

records.mechanism: Pre-hike sleep state gates Day-1 recovery architecture while Day-2 supercompensation remains durable

stimulus.day_2_pattern: AUTONOMIC_RESTORED returned on Day-2 despite Day-1 strain

physiological_response: Compromised pre-hike sleep drives Day-1 AUTONOMIC_STRAINED with elevated resting HR and suppressed HRV.
Day-2 recovery can still return to AUTONOMIC_RESTORED after the acute Day-1 sleep-gated cost.
Pre-hike REM and total sleep duration determine whether recovery appears immediately restored or delayed by 24 hours.
adaptation_outcomes: Sleep is a gate on Day-1 architecture rather than proof that the training load failed.
Day-2 supercompensation across Hikes 16-22 confirms durable recovery capacity.
Pre-hike sleep quality becomes a required context field for interpreting HRV and RHR after apex efforts.

supporting_science.finding: Sleep duration and quality are central determinants of athletic recovery and performance.
HRV monitoring can identify autonomic recovery status after endurance training.
Sleep is essential for athletic recovery and performance adaptation.
